issue_context.title: Gradually degrading performance of Ansible inventory handling on Ansible Core 2.14 and later, up to latest devel)
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Ansible Core versions 2.14.x and later (incl. various revisions of the `devel` branch up to today) show a worse and worse performance characteristic in combination with using the `ansible.builtin.constructed` inventory plugin.

I prepared a test case at https://github.com/cschug/ansible_issue in order to make this issue reproducible. This is a rather minimal and synthetic mockup as I cannot expose my live repository due to data privacy reasons which contains around 260 hosts in the inventory. The number of hosts in the test case is just 38 hosts, which is good enough to demonstrate the issue and also doesn't makes tests too painful.

In my life repository even simple things like `ansible all --list-hosts` take more than a minute now (was around 5 seconds with Ansible Core 2.13.4) . According to my analysis so far this is due to the massively increased number of file system operations, especially calls to `newfstatat` by more than a factor of 1,000.

I was able to identify at least two commits which made the situation really much worse. For full details please see https://github.com/cschug/ansible_issue/blob/main/README.md

Thank you

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### OS / Environment

Workstation hardware is Dell Precision 5820 Tower with Xeon W-2145 CPU, 64 GB of RAM and NVMe SSDs. It's not the youngest anymore but the specs should exceed the minimum requirements to run Ansible by far.

### Steps to Reproduce

Full test case at https://github.com/cschug/ansible_issue
```
$ git clone https://github.com/cschug/ansible_issue
$ time strace -c -e newfstatat ansible all --list-hosts
```


### Expected Results

- Times spend to handle the Ansible inventory (in combination with `ansible.builtin.constructed` inventory plugin) should be improved, ideally to bring it to a a level similar to Ansible Core 2.13.4 and before.
- Excessive number of file system calls should be reduced. Compared to Ansible 2.13.4 the current `devel` does more 1,000 times more calls of `newfstatat` as reported by `strace(8)`.

Hi All,

I also faced with this issue after upgrading from Ansible 6.4 to Ansible 7.2, in my case not with inventory but with regular playbooks.

I created a minimal playbook to demonstrate the issue.  In Ansible 6.4 (core 2.13.7) playbook execution takes ~3 seconds while in Ansible 7.1 & 7.2 (core 2.14.2) it takes 34 seconds.  https://pastebin.com/8KETYhaq
Measured with "time ansible-playbook -i localhost, -e ansible_connection=local -v"

After applying changes from @nitzmahone https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/79781/commits it became fast again.  Is it expected to have this fix in an upcoming ansible release?

Yes, we're planning on merging and backporting some form of those fixes to ansible-core 2.14- still some debate going on about a few implementation details, but I think what's in #79781 is probably what it will look like.

@bcoca @nitzmahone Is there any chance to get either https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/79650 or https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/79781 merged before Ansible Core 2.15 enters feature freeze which is due 2023-03-31 (i.e. in a few days) according the the [roadmap](https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/roadmap/ROADMAP_2_15.html)?

Many thanks in advance!

This issue still happens with ansible 7.5 / ansible-core 2.14.5.

It causes REAL slowness on regular playbooks which intensively use Jinja expressions, you don't need to do anything with dynamic inventories / inventory plugins, so maybe a more generic bug title would describe this issue better.

In your example regardless of the slowness introduced in ansible-core it might be worth looking into defining a custom filter plugin that would be responsible for the functionality that all those `replace` filter calls together provide and then using that custom filter in `map`, something like `active_events|map('my_custom_replaces_filter')|list` as opposed to running `set_fact` in a loop.

Thanks for your suggestion, I know that there are a lot of cases where data manipulation would be much easier in Python.  Unfortunately there are crazy limitations here and because of that I can't use custom plugins, just "plain" ansible playbooks.  This is only a synthetic example where the difference is significant, but there are a lot of scripts with similar constructs, so our ansible upgrade is delayed because of this issue.
We have the same problem with the latest release (ansible 8.3) also.
Barring any unforeseen issues, the fix for this will land in 2.15.5 and 2.14.11 (just missed the bus for 2.15.4 and 2.14.10).

review_comments: From the previous change where this override was copied in: a non-empty `collection_list` should be an error here (it's not even consulted right now, but as we refactor things down the line, want to make sure it never is, either)

Without any tests or code currently using this method, I'd suggest we just raise `NotImplementedError` or something if anything actually tries to call it (even if the code stays in place). Otherwise it's just going to rot and/or be an "attractive nuisance".
[bikeshed] suggest `j2_wrapper_cache` or `j2_plugin_cache` or something that's clearer that we're not caching the actual Python modules or something else

Doing the name lookup iteratively using `matches_name` without caching is even more expensive than what was happening before. It would be *waaay* cheaper to pre-fill the cache with multiple entries using the `ansible.builtin` and `ansible.legacy` prefixes as appropriate rather than looping over the entire cache and using  `matches_name`. A quick profile against the provided sample repro shows that it's now spending ~20% of the entire runtime in `matches_name` (and that'd be way worse for template-heavy playbooks). The extra memory cost of multiple entries is negligible, and makes this lookup O(1).

Might as well just pass the actual class type into the `Jinja2Loader` init at construction-time- it's never going to change for a given loader, has no performance impact (since we always have exactly 2, filters and tests) and let you get rid of all the dynamic class name and import stuff in `_load_jinja2_class` (which is fairly expensive).
